newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine guerrilla wants severe sentence.
newsitem.headline: Argentine guerrilla wants severe sentence.

text.p: Argentine guerrilla Enrique Gorriaran Merlo, on trial for a bloody 1989 attack on an army barracks, proclaimed himself unrepentant on Wednesday and demanded "the highest possible sentence."
Gorriaran Merlo and his ex-wife Ana Sivori, accused of being his accomplice in the attack, fired their lawyers a week ago saying they were already condemned.

They spent three hours on Wednesday justifying their actions before an Argentine court judging them for the country's last major guerrilla action, in which 39 people died, 60 were wounded and three were reported missing.
Earlier on Wednesday state prosecutors demanded a life sentence for Gorriaran and for Sivori. The court was due to give its sentence on Thursday.

Gorriaran, who also admitted to killing Nicaraguan dictator Anastasio Somoza in exile in Paraguay and was for years one of Latin America's most wanted men, told the court which was due to give its verdict:

"Given the characteristics of this tribunal, it would be humiliating if they did not give me the highest possible sentence," he said. "I am not going to join the indecent wave of repentant guerrillas."

Both he and Sivori contrasted their trial with the amnesty declared in 1989 for all the military personnel who took part in the "Dirty War" of the late 1970s in which at least 10,000 Argentines "disappeared" at the hands of death squads, and the amnesty for the guerrillas they fought.

"If I were someone who disappeared people, or a torturer or a murderer I would have been pardoned," said Gorriaran, while Sivori said: "If I were the wife of a soldier none of this would be happening."

The 55-year-old guerrilla was arrested after years on the run while walking along a street in Mexico. He alleges he was kidnapped by Mexican and Argentine secret service men and taken to Argentina illegally without extradition proceedings.
Gorriaran Merlo founded the Marxist People's Revolutionary Army (ERP), which carried out many bloody attacks and kidnaps in the 1970s. Later, he founded the All for the Fatherland Movement (MTP).
He admitted in media interviews before his capture that he planned and executed the assassination of Somoza in Paraguay in 1980.
The guerrilla leader argued that he carried out the assault on the Argentine army's La Tablada barracks to head off a threatened coup against the elected government of Raul Alfonsin.
